messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: Serving runtime crashloop detected on cluster-west-1 (svc: inference-runtime). Immediate on-call: Zoe Kim. Error rate spike >30% and a subset of pods are CrashLoopBackOff.
Zoe Kim: I'm on it. Initial hypothesis: segfaults in the custom kernel path after yesterday's runtime rollout.
Dan Walker: I'm seeing repeated SIGSEGV in runtime logs for v0.9.7-rc4. Paste of last few lines: 
```
2024-03-02T11:04:22Z runtime[pid=2145]: eva_kernel() +0x1a2
2024-03-02T11:04:22Z runtime[pid=2145]: segfault at 0 ip 00007f8a12b2c3d sp 00007fffa9c1e230 error 4 in libcustom_kernels.so[7f8a12a00000+13000]
2024-03-02T11:04:22Z runtime[pid=2145]: Container exited with status 139
```
Arun Patel: Confirmed. Also seeing CUDA memory accounting anomalies on the same timeline: repeated "CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS" and occasional OOM messages immediately prior to segfault. nvidia-smi shows memory spike then reset.
Priya Singh: Which clusters are impacted? Is this only hosted or also Dedicated?
Zoe Kim: cluster-west-1 and cluster-east-2 host pools showing CrashLoopBackOff. Dedicated pools with older runtime v0.9.6 are fine. So likely regression in v0.9.7-rc4 kernel paths.
OpsHeather: Customer impact: several API requests returned 502/ERR_CRASH or timed out. Telemetry shows increased latency and ~120 failing requests/min for three high-volume customers. We should page CS for status updates.
customer-success-bot: Notifying account owners for customers with >5% error increases: AcmeCorp, BrightHealth, NoteableApps.
Zoe Kim: Immediate mitigations I'm trying: 1) scale down concurrent replicas to reduce steady-state memory; 2) cordon and drain a small failure domain to collect coredumps; 3) roll back the runtime version for new pods.
Dan Walker: Suggest we temporarily route traffic to the fallback model variant (quantized, no custom kernels) using routing policy. That avoids the kernel codepath.
Arun Patel: Agreed. Steps I executed:
```
# mark node unschedulable for investigation
kubectl cordon gpu-node-17 -n prod
kubectl drain gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data -n prod
# set runtime rollout to 0.9.6 for svc inference-runtime
kubectl set image deploy/inference-runtime runtime=redwood/runtime:v0.9.6 -n prod
```
Arun Patel: After scaling and rollback, new pods are coming up with v0.9.6 and are healthy so far. Old crashlooping pods still in CrashLoopBackOff for investigation.
Zoe Kim: Capturing a coredump from one of the crashloop pods for analysis. Ran the following in the node where it crashed: 
```
sudo journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 | grep -i segfault
sudo mkdir -p /var/coredumps/incident-1712003456
sudo gcore -o /var/coredumps/incident-1712003456/runtime <pid>
# also copied /var/log/runtime.log and /usr/lib/libcustom_kernels.so
```
Priya Singh: Any need to escalate to runtime/ML eng (Arun/Dan)?
Zoe Kim: Arun/Dan are already on. We should also disable the custom kernel feature flag in the config map to prevent future pods from enabling the path: 
```
kubectl -n prod patch configmap/inference-config -p '{"data":{"enable_custom_kernels":"false"}}'
kubectl rollout restart deployment/inference-runtime -n prod
```
Dan Walker: I'll open a debug build to reproduce locally with the same seed inputs. If it's reproducible under ASAN/UBSAN we can pin the fault. Meanwhile, rollback + feature-flag disable + routing fallback should minimize customer impact.
OpsHeather: I'll draft an interim status update for the status page and send to customers: short notice, degraded serving in west/east, mitigations in progress, no data exfiltration. Putting ETA 30-60m.
Priya Singh: On-call handoff in ~20m. Zoe, can you add a concise summary to the thread so the next shift knows what's done and what's open?
Zoe Kim: Summary for handoff:
- Incident start: 2024-03-02T11:04:22Z (thread root)
- Symptom: CrashLoopBackOffs + SIGSEGV in libcustom_kernels.so for v0.9.7-rc4. Some nodes showed CUDA illegal address / OOM before segfault.
- Scope: cluster-west-1 & cluster-east-2, subset of pods serving hosted customers. Dedicated pools unaffected. ~3 customers with >5% error rate.
- Actions taken: rolled back deployment to v0.9.6, disabled enable_custom_kernels flag, routed traffic to fallback quantized model variant, cordoned and drained suspect node-17, collected coredumps & logs, notified CS.
- Current status: new pods on v0.9.6 healthy; error rate dropped to baseline (~1-2% transient). Crashlooping pods remain for analysis but traffic no longer hits the bad path.
- Outstanding: full gdb backtrace from coredump, reproduce in debug build, root cause (kernel memory use vs. CUDA driver mismatch).

Arun Patel: I'm working on reproducer and will upload ASAN logs to the incident bucket /incidents/1712003456. Expect initial root cause hypothesis in 2-4 hours.
Dan Walker: If we confirm it's a JIT or alignment bug in libcustom_kernels, we should also add a kernel compatibility test in CI to catch this on future releases.
OpsHeather: I posted the status page update: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/1712003456 - short message and link to this thread.
customer-success-bot: CS owners updated customers: AcmeCorp (on call), BrightHealth (email), NoteableApps (Slack).
Priya Singh: Thanks all. For the handoff: please leave any follow-ups in the thread. My notes will include links to coredump and the rollback PR.
Zoe Kim: Adding checklist for next on-call: confirm v0.9.6 pods remain stable for 1h, verify no regressions in latency/throughput, ensure coredump analysis is attached to the incident ticket.
Arun Patel: FYI captured environment info: CUDA driver 12.1.0, libcuda 520.x, runtime built against CUDA 12.2 - might be a driver/ABI mismatch on certain nodes. Investigating.
Dan Walker: Good catch. If ABI mismatch, we should patch node images or pin driver version in node pool and add preflight checks.
Priya Singh: I'll prepare a customer-facing postmortem skeleton once root cause is known.
OpsHeather: Marking this incident as mitigated for customer routing. Keeping P0 until root cause determined.
Zoe Kim: Handoff to Priya for next shift at 11:25Z. Leaving logs and pointers. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Mitigation applied, error rate returning to baseline. Incident still open for RCA.
